Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". input.description: Find webhook delivery and SSRF protection
input.prompt:
This is the "memos" repository (a note-taking app, Go backend). I need to find how the server sends outbound HTTP webhooks when content/memos change.

Find and report:
1. The function that actually performs the outbound HTTP webhook delivery (the code that makes the HTTP request/POST to an external URL). Give the exact file path and function name.
2. What protects that outbound request from being pointed at internal/private network addresses (SSRF protection) — e.g. any check that blocks private IPs, localhost, link-local, loopback, or uses a custom dialer/DNS resolver validation. Give the exact file path and function name.

Search for terms like "webhook", "Post", "http.Post", "dispatch", "SSRF", "private", "IsPrivate", "loopback", "127.0.0.1", "DialContext", etc. Report exact file paths and line numbers with code snippets.

content.text:
I have everything needed. Both answers live in the `internal/webhook` package.

## 1. Outbound HTTP webhook delivery

**File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go`
**Function:** `Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error` (lines 119–180)

This is the code that actually makes the outbound POST. It marshals the payload to JSON, builds the request, optionally adds HMAC-SHA256 Standard-Webhooks signature headers, and fires it:

```go
req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, bytes.NewBuffer(body))   // line 126
...
resp, err := safeClient.Do(req)                                                  // line 152
```

Supporting delivery machinery in the same file:
- `PostAsync` (lines 184–196) — enqueues onto a bounded channel `asyncPostQueue`.
- `init()` (lines 42–55) — spawns 4 worker goroutines that drain the queue and call `Post`.
- `safeClient` (lines 32–37) — the shared `*http.Client` whose `Transport.DialContext` is the SSRF guard (see below).

## 2. SSRF protection

The protection is layered, spanning both files in the package:

**Primary (dial-time) guard — File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go`
**Function:** `safeDialContext(ctx, network, addr)` (lines 57–77)

This is the real enforcement point. It is wired into `safeClient.Transport.DialContext` (line 35), so every webhook connection goes through it. It resolves the host via DNS at connection time and rejects any resolved IP in a reserved range — this placement specifically defeats DNS-rebinding (TOCTOU) attacks because the check happens on the actual IP being dialed:

```go
ips, err := net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost(ctx, host)          // line 65
for _, ipStr := range ips {
    if ip := net.ParseIP(ipStr); ip != nil && isReservedIP(ip) {
        return nil, errors.Errorf("webhook: connection to reserved/private IP address is not allowed")  // line 72
    }
}
```

**IP-range predicate — File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/validate.go`
**Function:** `isReservedIP(ip net.IP) bool` (lines 44–54)

Checks the IP against `reservedNetworks`, the parsed form of `reservedCIDRs` (lines 14–23), which covers IPv4 loopback `127.0.0.0/8`, RFC-1918 private (`10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`), link-local / cloud IMDS `169.254.0.0/16`, IPv6 loopback `::1/128`, IPv6 unique-local `fc00::/7`, and IPv6 link-local `fe80::/10`.

**Admission-time validation (secondary) — File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/validate.go`
**Function:** `ValidateURL(rawURL string) error` (lines 62–83)

Called when a webhook is created/updated (via the API service layer). It requires an absolute http/https URL and rejects any URL whose hostname resolves to a reserved IP, using the same `isReservedIP` predicate.

**Escape hatch:** A package-level flag `AllowPrivateIPs bool` (validate.go line 41) short-circuits `isReservedIP` to always return `false` when set, disabling SSRF protection entirely for self-hosted deployments that intentionally target local-network services.

### Note on a second, unrelated SSRF guard
There is a separate, independent implementation for link-preview/HTML-meta fetching at `/bench/home/work/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go` — `secureDialContext` (line 51) and its `isPrivateIP` helper (line ~105, using `ip.IsLoopback() || ip.IsPrivate() || ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || ip.IsUnspecified()`). That is for the HTML metadata getter, not the webhook path, but it is the other SSRF-protected outbound HTTP surface in the repo.

Delivery function — `Post` in `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go` (lines ~119–180) is where the outbound webhook actually executes: it builds the `POST` request to the external URL and fires it via `safeClient.Do(req)`. Delivery is fanned out through `PostAsync`/worker goroutines, but every request ultimately runs through `Post` using the shared `safeClient`.

Protection mechanism — SSRF protection is enforced at dial time by `safeDialContext` in `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go` (lines ~57–77), which is wired into `safeClient.Transport.DialContext`. It resolves the target host and rejects any connection whose resolved IP falls in a reserved/private range, using `isReservedIP` in `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/validate.go` (lines ~44–54, matching the `reservedCIDRs` covering loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS `169.254.0.0/16`, IPv6 ULA/link-local, etc.). Because the check runs on the actual dialed IP, it also defeats DNS-rebinding. A secondary admission-time check, `ValidateURL` (`validate.go`, ~62–83), applies the same predicate when a webhook URL is created/updated. (A package flag `AllowPrivateIPs` can disable this for self-hosted setups.)

**Answer:**
- delivery function — `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; protection mechanism — `safeDialContext` (backed by `isReservedIP` in `internal/webhook/validate.go`) — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`
